prompt_en: In an incense village's drying yard, hundreds of incense stick bundles fan out across the brick yard, while a worker sits tying another bundle.
refined_prompt: In an incense village's drying yard, hundreds of incense stick bundles fan out across the brick yard, while a worker sits tying another bundle. In the village of Làng Hương, hundreds of bó chân hương, or bundles of sandalwood incense sticks, are meticulously arranged on brick beds in the drying yard. Each bundle, resembling a small temple pagoda, stands as a symbol of the harmony between man and nature in Vietnamese spirituality. The sticks are smooth and have a golden-brown color that complements the natural surroundings, creating a picturesque sight. The yard buzzes with the earthy scent of sandalwood and the subtle sounds of gentle rustling as the wind carries the fragrance across the village. Artisans carefully manage the drying process to ensure the sticks burn evenly and release a consistent, soothing aroma during rituals. These sticks are indispensable during Lunar New Year and Mid-Autumn Festival celebrations, where they are used to honor ancestors and invoke blessings.
